chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ali ibn Al-Nu'man, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abdul-A'la, who said:

I saw Umm Farwa performing Tawaf around the Kaaba, wearing a cloak and disguised. She touched the Stone with her left hand. A man among those performing Tawaf said to her, 'O maid of Allah, you have deviated from the Sunnah.' She said, 'We are in no need of your knowledge.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Umm Farwa's response 'We are in no need of your knowledge' regarding her deviation from the Sunnah in Tawaf?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Umm Farwa (a prominent companion of Imam al-Sadiq) demonstrates that while right-hand contact with the Black Stone is the established Sunnah, using the left hand does not invalidate the Tawaf, reflecting the Shia principle of distinguishing between recommended acts (Mustahabb) and obligatory ones (Wajib). Her witty retort, 'We are rich in your knowledge,' underscores the scholarly tradition of valuing deep, contextual understanding over rigid, superficial adherence to ritual details, a view supported by scholars like Al-Shaykh al-Mufid who note that deviation from the Sunnah in this specific act does not nullify the pilgrimage.
